explanation: Smart pointers in C++ are template classes that manage dynamic memory automatically, ensuring proper resource deallocation and preventing memory leaks. They are used to implement RAII (Resource Acquisition Is Initialization) idioms, providing safer and more expressive memory management compared to raw pointers. Modern C++ emphasizes the use of smart pointers to handle ownership semantics explicitly, with std::unique_ptr for exclusive ownership and std::shared_ptr for shared ownership scenarios.
syntax:
std::unique_ptr<Type> ptr = std::make_unique<Type>(constructor_args); // for exclusive ownership
std::shared_ptr<Type> sptr = std::make_shared<Type>(constructor_args); // for shared ownership
example_explanation: This example demonstrates the use of modern C++ smart pointers: std::unique_ptr manages a Widget instance with exclusive ownership, automatically destroying it when it goes out of scope. std::shared_ptr manages shared ownership of a Widget, with reference counting ensuring the object is destroyed only when the last shared_ptr is destroyed. This showcases how smart pointers facilitate safe, automatic resource management aligned with modern C++ best practices.
